audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3..6].side all read Skill while win[3..6] read Ziggs, Anivia, Anivia, Anivia; the packet chart agrees with win[].
audit.why: Four rows rendering two different answers. 48.55% over 795 games with a losing early and a winning post-6 matches the packet chart exactly.
Level 6 is the real inversion: Glacial Storm clears instantly and outlasts his poke, while Mega Inferno Bomb is 120s at rank 1 so his own 6 spike is a once-a-wave event.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors repeated across four fields: the poke is attributed to a 'W-E combo' that 'outranges your Q Flash Frost entirely', and the passive is called 'short-fuse bombs' that punish minion clearing.
audit.why: Riot data: Flash Frost is 1075 — longer than Satchel Charge (1000), Hexplosive Minefield (900) and Bouncing Bomb (850). He does not outrange you; he out-paces you, because Bouncing Bomb is 6s at rank 1 against your 11s stun. Short Fuse is an empowered basic attack whose cooldown drops with every ability cast, not a bomb. Satchel Charge is a 20s knockback that displaces Ziggs too, which is why it is his escape.
audit.corrected: Reframed as a volume-and-safety problem, not a range problem, and named Bouncing Bomb, Hexplosive Minefield and Short Fuse correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere (sequencingCues 0).
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb 6s, Hexplosive Minefield 16s, Satchel Charge 20s, Mega Inferno Bomb 120s at rank 1 — the mines and the satchel are the two windows that decide whether a step-up is free.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten as wait-for-X-then-Y with all four numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing claims Satchel Charge bypasses stacking resistances (percentHealth flag).
audit.why: Riot's own text for Satchel Charge says only magic damage and a knockback — no percent-health component. Per the flag-versus-description rule, the description wins.
audit.corrected: Not written to the page. The Short Fuse auto-reset tell from the same entry IS real and was added.

edits.before: Ziggs wins by landing Satchel Charge, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Ziggs wins by out-shoving you, mining every approach, and satchelling you off the wave whenever you step up.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - W Crystallize is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge: 20s at rank 1 — it knocks him away as well as you, so step up only once it is spent. - Bouncing Bomb is 6s and Hexplosive Minefield 16s: walk in after the mines, never before. - Mega Inferno Bomb is 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by taking the ground he needs — Glacial Storm turns his 850-range poke into a choice between farming and living.

edits.before: Ziggs whiffs Satchel Charge and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: With Satchel spent he has no escape — wall the lane and walk in.

edits.before: That is Ziggs’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Short Fuse hands him a free empowered auto after every cast.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: His proximity mines detonate on contact and slow — path around the minefield, not through it.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Ziggs walks straight at you.
edits.after: Mega Inferno Bomb reaches 5000 units — with the egg down, sitting low anywhere on the map is a free kill for him.

edits.before: Ziggs' superior poke range lets him chip you freely at level 1-2 with no way for you to answer.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb is back every 6s at rank 1, so he chips you freely at 1-2 while your stun waits 11s.

edits.before: The W-E poke war keeps compounding his lead through levels 3-5 since your kit lacks the range to retaliate.
edits.after: Hexplosive Minefield slows you off the wave through levels 3-5, and Short Fuse turns every cast into a free auto.

edits.before: Same outranged dynamic continues through level 5 as he shoves waves and pokes without risk.
edits.after: Same pattern through level 5 — he clears the wave from 850 range and never has to step up.

edits.before: Ziggs' W-E poke combo outranges your Q Flash Frost entirely, letting him shove waves and chip your HP from safety while satchel-charging any egg you try to hatch near the wave.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb every 6s and a 16s Hexplosive Minefield let him shove and chip from safety, and Satchel Charge knocks you clean out of position the moment you step up to answer.

edits.before: Ziggs' W-E combo has more range than your Flash Frost and hits significantly harder in the early poke war, letting him chip your HP freely while you struggle to land anything back. His passive short-fuse bombs punish minion-clearing attempts, and satchel charge gives him a safe escape or extra poke whenever you try to close the gap. Play very passive, hug tower, and don't contest CS aggressively — you're just surviving the poke phase until your ultimate comes online.
edits.after: Your Flash Frost reaches further than anything he owns at 1075, but Bouncing Bomb returns every 6 seconds and your stun does not, so he wins the early poke war on sheer volume. Short Fuse empowers his next auto and speeds up with every ability he casts, and Satchel Charge gives him a safe escape or extra poke whenever you try to close the gap. Play very passive, hug tower, and don't contest CS aggressively — you're just surviving the poke phase until your ultimate comes online.

edits.before: Farm safely under tower and avoid walking into W-E poke range
edits.after: Farm under tower and stay off the minefield he drops on the wave

edits.before: Poke relentlessly with W-E before you can retaliate with equal range
edits.after: Spam Bouncing Bomb on its 6s timer before your stun comes back

edits.before: Shove waves fast and threaten your tower with W splash damage
edits.after: Shove fast and hexplode your tower plates with Satchel Charge

notes: Central correction: the page told the reader Ziggs outranges Anivia. He does not — Flash Frost is 1075, against Satchel 1000, Minefield 900 and Bouncing Bomb 850. His edge is cadence (6s Q vs your 11s stun) and the self-displacing 20s escape, so the advice changes from 'you can never reach him' to 'you can reach him, just not on his schedule'. Short Fuse is an empowered auto, not a bomb. Packet suspectName 'Glacial Storm's' is a false positive — that is Anivia's own R. I did NOT write the _missing 'Satchel Charge bypasses resistances' line: Riot's text has no percent-health component, so the derived flag looks like a tooltip-parse misfire. Level chart squared to the packet on the last four rows.
